title: 2025 AMC 10B Problem 19

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement:
A container has a \(1 \times 1\) square bottom, a \(3 \times 3\) open square top, and four congruent trapezoidal sides, as shown. Starting when the container is empty, a hose that runs water at a constant rate takes \(35\) minutes to fill the container up to the midline of the trapezoids.

How many more minutes will it take to fill the remainder of the container?

solutions.text: The container is a square frustum: a horizontal slice at height fraction \(t\) has side \(1 + 2t.\) Extend the sides up to their apex, and the volume out to where the side length is \(w\) scales as \(w^3.\) So the whole container is \(3^3 - 1^3 = 26\) parts, the piece up to the midline (side \(2\)) is \(2^3 - 1^3 = 7\) parts, and the rest is \(3^3 - 2^3 = 19\) parts. Those \(7\) parts take \(35\) minutes, so each part is \(5\) minutes. The remaining \(19\) parts take \(95\) minutes. Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: The container is a piece of a pyramid; the volume from the apex up to side length \(w\) scales as \(w^3\)
Volumes split as \(2^3 - 1^3 = 7\) (up to the midline, side \(2\)) and \(3^3 - 2^3 = 19\) (remainder); scale the \(35\) minutes
